name: My roof is flat or low-slope. What special issues should I watch out for?

mainEntity.name: My roof is flat or low-slope. What special issues should I watch out for?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Flat and low-slope roofs are more prone to **ponding water, membrane damage, and drainage issues**, so they need closer monitoring than steep shingle roofs. Small problems on flat roofs can spread quickly.

Instead of shedding water quickly, flat roofs rely on correctly sloped surfaces and drains or scuppers. Any clogs, low spots, or seam failures can lead to leaks.

Key factors:
- Ponding water after 48 hours with no rain
- Cracked, blistered, or punctured membrane areas
- Clogged drains, scuppers, or gutters
- Poor flashing at HVAC units, skylights, or parapet walls

Schedule regular inspections and keep drains cleared, especially before and after rainy season. If you see standing water or soft, spongy spots, have a roofer look immediately; catching issues early can prevent expensive interior repairs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Flat and low-slope roofs need extra attention for ponding water, membrane cracks or blisters, and clogged drains or scuppers. Monitor them at least yearly and after heavy rain, and call a roofer quickly if you see standing water or soft spots to avoid costly leaks and interior damage.
